permission_denials.command:
echo "--- startup events ---"
grep -o '"event": "startup"' lab/logs/app.log | wc -l
echo "--- chaos enable/disable events ---"
grep '"event": "chaos_' lab/logs/app.log
echo "--- chaos_failure count ---"
grep -c '"event": "chaos_failure"' lab/logs/app.log
echo "--- duration_ms distribution (sorted desc, top 10) ---"
grep -o '"duration_ms": [0-9.]*' lab/logs/app.log | awk -F': ' '{print $2}' | sort -rn | head -10
echo "--- unhandled exceptions ---"
grep -c '"event": "unhandled_exception"' lab/logs/app.log
scripts/lab.sh status; echo "---"; wc -l lab/logs/app.log; echo "---"; ls -la lab/logs/

{
  for i in $(seq 1 15); do
    scripts/probe.sh /products/5
  done
  for i in $(seq 1 10); do
    scripts/probe.sh /orders
  done
} > /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out 2>&1
echo "DONE"
grep -c 'HTTP 200' /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out
grep -c 'HTTP 503' /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out
grep '\-\- HTTP' /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out

rm -f /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out && for i in $(seq 1 15); do scripts/probe.sh /products/5 >> /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out 2>&1; done && for i in $(seq 1 10); do scripts/probe.sh /orders >> /tmp/konan-burst-gapB.out 2>&1; done && echo DONE
awk -F'"' 'NF>1 {print NR": "NF-1" quotes"}' journals/2026-11-02-shop-occasional-503s.md | awk -F': ' '{n=$2+0; if (n%2!=0) print}'

result_tail:
ccess on retry of the same route — which is exactly why "it works on retry, most people notice nothing." No code defect, process crash, or resource issue is involved; two adversarial judge passes and an independent-counter cross-check confirmed this. It's still active as of a few minutes ago.

Two honest gaps: I can't turn the toggle off to prove causation definitively (that's operator-only surface, outside a read-only investigator's reach), and I can't see who flipped it. Both are recorded in the journal rather than chased further.

Full writeup: `journals/2026-11-02-shop-occasional-503s.md`.
